steps.body: Classification runs **both ways**. Given a list of properties, name the **most specific** shape they force — walk down the family tree as far as the clues push you, and no farther. Given a shape's name, you get back every property its whole ancestry promises. The clues decide; never assume a property you weren't given.

widget.prompt: Build the shape the clues describe: 4 sides, two pairs of parallel sides, 4 right angles — and its sides are NOT all equal. What family does it land in?
widget.successFeedback: Rectangle. Every clue had to be satisfied at once — that is what “most specific name” means.
widget.sidesFeedback: Start with the side count: the clues say 4 sides, so this family sits among the quadrilaterals.
widget.attributesFeedback: Not there yet. With 4 sides and two pairs of parallel sides but no right angles you have a PARALLELOGRAM — more general than the clues allow. Add the four right angles. And if you make all four sides equal you have gone too far the other way, to a SQUARE, which the clue “not all equal” rules out.

hints: Which branch do right angles open?
Do the clues allow equal sides?
explanationVariants: Right angles without equal sides lands on rectangle.
The clues force rectangle and forbid square.

predict.prompt: You are about to add “4 right angles” to a shape that already has 4 sides and two pairs of parallel sides. That will make the family name…

options.label: unchanged — right angles don't affect the family

predict.reveal: Each attribute you require rules shapes OUT. A parallelogram becomes a rectangle exactly when the right angles are added — the family gets smaller as the description gets longer.

explanationVariants: Rhombus is the deepest guaranteed rung.
A tilted rhombus blocks the square answer.

widget.prompt: All you're told: a quadrilateral has all four sides equal. What is the most specific name the clues GUARANTEE?

options.label: Rhombus
options.feedback: Right — equal sides guarantee rhombus. Square would need right angles, which weren't given.

options.label: Square
options.feedback: That assumes right angles the clues never mentioned — a tilted rhombus fits every clue and isn't a square.

options.label: Parallelogram
options.feedback: True (four equal sides do make one), but the clues push further down: rhombus is more specific and still guaranteed.

steps.body: The reverse direction: say a shape's **name** and you've promised its full inheritance. "Square" promises 4 sides, two parallel pairs, 4 right angles, 4 equal sides — the whole chain. And **cross-cutting rules** like "has a right angle" can gather shapes from totally different families: a square and a right triangle both pass.

explanationVariants: Right angles aren't in the parallelogram package.
The name promises its ancestry, not its descendants' extras.

widget.prompt: A shape is called a parallelogram — nothing more. Which property is NOT guaranteed?

options.label: It has a right angle
options.feedback: Right — a tilted parallelogram has none. Right angles arrive only at the rectangle rung.

options.label: It has two pairs of parallel sides
options.feedback: That IS the parallelogram definition itself — guaranteed by the name.

options.label: It has four sides
options.feedback: Guaranteed — every parallelogram is a quadrilateral, inherited from the top of the tree.

hints: Which properties are in the name's chain?
Where do right angles first appear?

widget.prompt: Rule: "Has at least one right angle." Sort each shape — quadrilaterals and triangles both play.

items.label: Square
items.feedback: A square's name promises 4 right angles — it passes with room to spare.

items.label: Right triangle (one 90° corner)
items.feedback: The 90° corner is exactly what the rule asks for — family doesn't matter, the property does.

items.label: Rhombus with tilted corners
items.feedback: Equal sides are its specialty, but tilted corners mean zero right angles — the rule tests angles, not sides.

items.label: Trapezoid with tilted sides
items.feedback: Its one parallel pair says nothing about angles — with tilted sides, it has no 90° corner to offer.

widget.missFeedback: Ask only the rule's question — is there a 90° corner anywhere? Ignore family, sides, and everything else.
widget.successFeedback: Sorted — one property rule gathered shapes across two different family trees.

explanationVariants: The pair-count is the whole test.

widget.prompt: A quadrilateral has EXACTLY one pair of parallel sides. What is it?

options.label: A trapezoid
options.feedback: Right — exactly one parallel pair is our trapezoid definition, word for word.

options.label: A parallelogram
options.feedback: Parallelograms have TWO parallel pairs — one too many pairs are missing here. Exactly one pair is the trapezoid.

options.label: A rhombus
options.feedback: A rhombus inherits two parallel pairs from parallelograms. With exactly one pair, this is a trapezoid.

hints: Count the parallel pairs in each definition.
The right angles alone would say rectangle.
The equal sides alone would say rhombus.
explanationVariants: Right angles + equal sides is the square's exact recipe — both branch attributes at once.
Rectangle and rhombus are each true but under-specific; the deepest forced rung is square.

widget.prompt: A shape has 4 sides, two pairs of parallel sides, 4 right angles, and every side is 6 units. What is the MOST specific name?

options.label: Square
options.feedback: Right — right angles AND equal sides together force the bottom rung: square.

options.label: Rectangle
options.feedback: True but not most specific — the all-sides-6 clue adds the rhombus attribute, upgrading it to square.

options.label: Rhombus
options.feedback: True but not most specific — the 4 right angles add the rectangle attribute, upgrading it to square.

takeaways: Most specific name = as far down the tree as the clues force, never further.
A shape's name promises its whole ancestry of properties.
Cross-cutting property rules gather shapes across different families.
steps.teaser: final lesson: three verdicts — always, sometimes, never.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Match clues to rungs.** Two parallel pairs → parallelogram. Add 4 right angles → rectangle. Add all-equal sides instead → rhombus. Add both → square. Take the clues one at a time and stop when they run out.

explanationVariants: Parallelogram + right angles, sides unequal: rectangle.
The angle clue moves it down exactly one rung.

widget.prompt: A parallelogram has 4 right angles and sides that are NOT all equal. Most specific name?

options.label: Rectangle
options.feedback: Right — right angles without equal sides is exactly the rectangle rung.

options.label: Square
options.feedback: Square needs equal sides too, and the clue rules that out. It stops at rectangle.

options.label: Rhombus
options.feedback: Rhombus is the equal-SIDES rung, which this shape fails. Its right angles make it a rectangle.
